title_original: ‘Artificial’ Writer Simon Rich Boards Oscar-Qualified Sci-Fi Short ‘Houston, We Have a Crush’ as Executive Producer (EXCLUSIVE)

blocks.text: “Artificial” screenwriter Simon Rich has joined the short film “Houston, We Have a Crush” as executive producer.

Directed by Omer Ben-Shachar and co-written with New Yorker humorist Jennifer Kim, the live-action short follows Ditto, a lonely alien who discovers a phone accidentally left behind by an astronaut. As he explores its contents, Ditto develops an all-consuming crush on the phone’s owner.

blocks.text: The New Yorker has acquired the sci-fi project for an upcoming premiere on its digital platforms, including YouTube.
Rich is a frequent contributor to The New Yorker. His other credits include “Saturday Night Live,” “Man Seeking Woman,” “Inside Out” and “Miracle Workers.”

“I’m thrilled to present this hilarious and heartbreaking short directed by the brilliant Omer Ben-Shachar,” Rich said in a statement on Friday. “Co-written by Ben-Shachar and Jen Kim, ‘Houston, We Have a Crush’ is a brutally relatable story of loneliness and unrequited love that speaks to the freakish alien bird in all of us. I’m so glad a movie this strange and this beautiful exists and I can’t wait to see what Omer and Jen create next.”

“Houston, We Have a Crush” has screened at more than 40 film festivals worldwide, including Palm Springs International ShortFest, NewFest, Guadalajara, Austin, Urbanworld, Indy Shorts, HollyShorts and SXSW Sydney, where it was nominated for best narrative short. Its accolades include the Art Directors Guild (ADG, IATSE Local 800) Production Design Award at the GuadaLAjara Film Festival, the Jury Award for best fanomenon short at the Leeds International Film Festival and best international short film at the 43rd Sulmona Film Festival.

“Jen and I thought it would be funny if an astronaut accidentally left his phone in space, and an alien found it and fell in love with him based on what was inside,” said Ben-Shachar. “But the idea came from something very personal. We’ve both experienced that feeling of projecting our fantasies onto someone we barely know, only to discover that the person we’ve imagined doesn’t quite exist. We wanted to explore that very human experience through the eyes of an alien who, in many ways, feels just like us.”

The film stars Sam Humphrey as Ditto and Ben Rigby as the astronaut. Jason Eisner produced, with Bara Kim coproducing. In addition to Rich, executive producers include Hollywood Ventures Group, Claudio Olachea and Kim.

Ben-Shachar previously directed “Tree #3,” which won a Student Academy Award and received a Student Emmy nomination. His short “Single Residence Occupancy” won Imagine Entertainment’s “From Minutes to Movies ShortFest” and the Atlanta Film Festival’s Jury Award for Best Narrative Short. His films have screened at more than 100 festivals internationally, with previous work featured on Short of the Week and Vimeo Staff Picks.
The short is currently being developed as a feature film.
